ideas.title: top clone from /proc

Read /proc/<pid>/stat: utime and stime (fields 14 and 15) are CPU ticks. The name in () may contain spaces, so split after the last ")".

ideas.title: traceroute in Python
ideas.desc: Send probes with rising TTL and read the ICMP replies from each router on the way.
learn: IP TTL field and ICMP "Time Exceeded"
steps: Open a UDP socket for sending and a raw ICMP socket (SOCK_RAW, IPPROTO_ICMP) for receiving.
For ttl 1 to 30: set IP_TTL on the UDP socket and send to the target on port 33434 + ttl.
Wait up to 2 s on the ICMP socket; the reply's sender address is that hop.
ICMP type 11 = Time Exceeded (keep going); type 3 = Destination Unreachable (you arrived).
Measure round-trip time, 3 probes per hop.
Reverse-lookup each hop with socket.gethostbyaddr (it may fail; handle it).
Compare with the real traceroute.

ideas.title: Packet sniffer (AF_PACKET)
ideas.desc: Capture frames and decode Ethernet, IPv4 and TCP/UDP headers yourself, like a mini tcpdump.
learn: Ethernet, IPv4 and TCP header layouts
steps: socket.socket(socket.AF_PACKET, socket.SOCK_RAW, socket.ntohs(3)) receives every frame.
Ethernet header (14 bytes): destination MAC, source MAC, ethertype (0x0800 = IPv4).
IPv4 header: header length = IHL * 4, protocol (6 = TCP, 17 = UDP), source and destination IP.
TCP header: ports, seq, ack, data offset, flags (SYN, ACK, FIN, RST, PSH).
Print one line per packet: time, src:port > dst:port, flags, length.
Add filters: --port 80, --host 1.2.3.4.

ideas.title: Recursive DNS resolver with cache
ideas.desc: Resolve names yourself starting from the root servers, with caching.
learn: DNS message format (from your DNS query tool)
Referrals: NS records plus "glue" A records
steps: Start from a root server IP: 198.41.0.4 (a.root-servers.net).
Send the query without the recursion-desired flag; parse the answer, authority and additional sections.
Answer present → return it. Referral → pick an NS that has a glue IP and ask it.
NS without glue → resolve the NS name first (recursion).
Follow CNAMEs.
Cache every record until now + TTL; check the cache first.
Serve on UDP 127.0.0.1:5353 and test with dig @127.0.0.1 -p 5353 example.com.

ideas.title: Distributed job queue
ideas.desc: Reliable background jobs with retries, backoff and a dead-letter queue.
learn: Postgres FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED (or Redis lists/streams)
steps: API: POST /jobs {type, payload} returns an id; GET /jobs/{id} returns its status.
Jobs table: status (queued, running, done, failed), attempts, run_at, locked_until.
Workers: SELECT ... WHERE status='queued' AND run_at <= now() FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED LIMIT 1.
Set locked_until = now + 30 s; if a worker dies, the job becomes visible again.
On failure: attempts += 1, run_at = now + 2^attempts seconds + random jitter.
After 5 attempts mark it dead and log an alert.

Phase 2 (backfill): copy existing rows with INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE in batches while live traffic continues, using updated_at to avoid overwriting newer rows.
Phase 3 (verify): compute count and an md5 checksum over ordered ids on both shards for that logical shard and compare; retry the backfill until they match.
Phase 4 (cutover): atomically switch reads and writes to the target, keep dual writes briefly, then stop writing to the source.
Phase 5 (cleanup): delete the logical shard rows from the source after a safety delay.
Run a load generator doing 500 writes per second during a move and prove no write is lost by comparing the generator's log with final data.
Kill the rebalance process in the middle and make it resume from the saved state without duplicates.

ideas.title: Mini stream processor with checkpointed exactly-once effects

Operator state and why it must be checkpointed together with the offset
Atomic checkpoint writes: write temp file, fsync, os.replace
Chandy-Lamport style snapshot idea (what Flink checkpoints do)
steps: Write gen_log.py: 1 million JSON events to events.log (user, ad, event_time) and a reader that can start at any offset.
Implement a tumbling-window counter operator with in-memory state and a watermark.
Every 10000 events write a checkpoint {offset, state, emitted_windows} to checkpoint.tmp, fsync, then os.replace to checkpoint.json.
Sink: write results into SQLite with INSERT OR REPLACE keyed (window_start, ad_id).
On startup load checkpoint.json, seek to its offset, and continue.
Crash test: kill -9 the process at random moments in a loop until the log is fully processed.
Compare the final SQLite table with the result of an uninterrupted run: it must be identical.
Break it on purpose: write the checkpoint before the sink commit, or skip fsync, and find the duplicate or missing counts.

ideas.title: Ride-matching simulator
ideas.desc: Simulate thousands of drivers and riders on a map and match them by cell lookup, ETA and offer timeouts.

Redis GEO or an in-memory grid for the latest driver position
Atomic locks (SET NX EX) to prevent double assignment
Matching as a ranking problem: ETA, rating, idle time
